title: MEMORY != LEARNING
hypothesis: If cumulative learning is real at the software architecture level, storing causal boundaries and scars should improve future decisions beyond raw memory volume alone.

groups.A_raw_memory: Retain raw prior episodes only; nearest-match retrieval allowed; no compressed rule extraction or causal credit.
groups.B_compressed_rules: Retain compressed rules extracted from prior episodes; no scars, boundaries, or causal credit.
groups.C_no_cumulative_memory: No cross-task memory; solve each task from current evidence only.
groups.D_verified_experience: Retain rules + failure scars + transfer boundaries + causal credit with provenance.

anti_leakage: training/development episodes and hidden/OOD episodes use disjoint seeds
hidden family parameters are unavailable to selectors
future-task outcomes are never used to compile memory
group D causal credit may use only completed prior episodes
benchmark code must log exact memory object used per decision
falsification_conditions: D does not beat C on aggregate hidden regret
D gain disappears after equal decision-budget control
D improvement is explained solely by larger memory footprint without efficiency gain
D has materially higher negative-transfer or repeat-failure rate
observed group ordering is unstable across fresh seed banks
claim_limit: A positive result would support cumulative software-level learning from verified experience in this benchmark only. It would not prove neural learning, AGI, or superintelligence.
